shorts.title: Same guest. Second commission.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: What did that second stay actually cost?
shorts.description: An illustrative small-inn story about the second commission on a guest the inn already knows. The full episode follows the calculation and the service someone could build around it.
shorts.pinned_comment: The full episode works through what the second stay costs—and who could get paid to prevent that cost. Open the related video.

shorts.title: The drafting got cheap. The judgment didn’t.
shorts.description: A fictional, test-only workflow showing actual drafting and scheduling tools. Drafts await human review; no messages are sent. The full episode explains the decisions the person still owns.
shorts.pinned_comment: The software can draft and schedule. The full episode shows the judgment that makes the service useful. Open the related video.

shorts.title: The inn served the guest. It doesn’t have his email.
shorts.description: The guest relationship creates a constraint before the inn chooses an email tool. The full episode follows what has to come first.
shorts.pinned_comment: An email tool doesn’t solve the first problem. The full episode explains what the inn needs before automation can work. Open the related video.

shorts.title: The big commission bill is the wrong number.
shorts.cliffhanger_line: What can this inn actually afford?
shorts.description: The episode’s illustrative $105K–$130K annual commission total is not the recoverable opportunity. The spoken 18–22% assumption remains qualified in this Short. The full episode calculates the smaller number that matters.
shorts.pinned_comment: The total commission bill is only the starting point. The full calculation shows what can shift and what a recovery service could charge. Open the related video.
